calibration: auto-data.net "Kerb Weight" is the DIN figure (driver excluded). Established against two makers who state their own convention: Hyundai i20 1140 "inkl. 75 kg Fahrergewicht" vs auto-data 1065; SEAT Leon 1316 "[with driver]" vs auto-data 1241. auto-data "Max. weight" matching the maker gross weight confirms the variant.
calibration_caveat: auto-data.net is USUALLY DIN but NOT always: it gave the EU figure for the pre-facelift SEAT Leon Mk3 (1305, matching SEAT), and for the Alfa Giulietta printed 1395 -- above Alfa own with-driver 1385. Reliable test: auto-data kerb exactly 75 below the maker with-driver figure AND auto-data "Max. weight" equal to the maker gross weight. Further counter-example: for the Nissan Qashqai J11 auto-data printed a kerb minimum 55 kg BELOW Nissan own no-driver figure -- neither convention. Note also Nissan CHANGED convention between generations: the J12 (2021+) brochure defines kerb weight per Dir. 92/21/95/48 as including 68 kg driver + 7 kg luggage, while the 2014 J11 brochure says "without driver".
massOk_flag: specs carrying massOk:1 have a source that states its own convention; tools/fit.js skips the EU-mass heuristic for them, because it still fires on some verified cars and a check that cries wolf stops being read
